status: Pilot content review; no psychometric equivalence or validated score claim

sources.purpose: Interests, abilities and knowledge are distinct constructs.
O*NET31 specific-interest descriptors include AI/Expert provenance; retain original rating/source/date.

rules.scope: 24 original concepts across12 proposed domains are not an official O*NET instrument. Broad correlation remains from official six-score instrument only.
rules.specificInterest: Occupation-specificInterest ratings describe occupations. They can guide reviewed general-interest content mapping; they do not measure a student or confirm a defining occupational responsibility.
rules.knowledge: Only use knowledge for explanation, relevant subject context and optional learning routes. Preference answers must never be scored as demonstrated knowledge.
rules.abilities: Only use abilities for transparent occupation descriptions or separately measured/self-reported strength clues. A love preference is not an ability score; never use these links to infer a ceiling.
rules.absence: Published app descriptors are truncated topN. Absence from a list is unknown/not selected, not zero or a demonstrated negative relation.
rules.coverage: Cap two related prompts as one domain. Require independent reviewed context/method domains for stronger evidence. Keep positive, contrary, unfamiliar/unanswered distinct.
rules.rank: If a prototype uses these mappings to order discovery, label it experimental general-interest connection, not statistical correlation, aptitude or confirmed profession match.
rules.criticalRestriction: No generic underlying-interest item can alone confirm a profession-specific responsibility. Initial content pairs need comprehension/pilot/reliability review.

facets.title: Understanding systems

questions.prompt: When something behaves unexpectedly, would you enjoy finding out what caused it?
Would tracing how different parts affect one another hold your attention?

facets.interpretation: Generic causal interest crosses physical, social, biological and computational systems. No single O*NET specific-interest area measures this. Require named occupation tasks/context before it supports a profession; use as invitation/explanation until reviewed task links exist.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Testing explanations

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy comparing two explanations by trying a fair test?
When evidence disagrees, would you want to investigate what could explain the difference?

facets.interpretation: Experimental/evidential preference is a method, not a scientific subject or competence. Can describe general evidence-seeking interest, not confirm medicine/engineering/legal practice. A separate reviewed task link is needed for occupation-level ranking.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Quantitative patterns

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy using a graph or numbers to see a pattern that is hard to notice?
Would building a simple model to compare possible outcomes interest you?

facets.interpretation: Closest semantic mapping to Mathematics/Statistics specific interest. General numerical/modeling interest can support broad quantitative connection. It does not establish mathematical ability or any specific analytical profession.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Design and constraints

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy inventing several ways to make something work within limits?
Would you want to compare a design's trade-offs and improve one aspect without losing another?

facets.interpretation: These are plausible design-method links but broad scenarios do not identify aesthetic/user-centered product design versus technical function. Keep one design domain; no independent double credit for the two items, and no automatic industrial-design/engineering confirmation.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Spatial/material exploration

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy picturing how parts or spaces might fit together?
Would shaping or carefully assembling materials be satisfying to you?

facets.interpretation: Split interpretation: picturing geometry and enjoying manual assembly are distinct. Neither answer measures spatial/manual ability. Spatial enjoyment alone must not imply liking heavy physical labor; material enjoyment must not infer engineering analysis.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Creative expression

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy finding an original way to communicate an idea or feeling?
Would you want to try several versions until a piece expresses what you mean?

facets.interpretation: General expressive iteration; medium remains unknown. May support creative exploration but cannot confirm writing, music, acting, graphic design or illustration independently. Ask medium/context before specialty confirmation.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Direct personal support

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy listening closely while someone works through a difficulty?
Would helping someone feel safer or more comfortable be rewarding?

facets.interpretation: Social Service is the closest broad content link. Health Care Service is only contextual and must require actual health interest, not kindness. No diagnosis, distress tolerance, clinical care, counseling competence, or willingness for intimate bodily care is inferred.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Explanation and learning

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy making a confusing idea easier for someone to understand?
Would adapting your explanation after someone gets stuck interest you?

facets.interpretation: Teaching/Education has strong semantic relevance; general preference to explain can support education exploration. Does not identify age group, subject, classroom setting, developmental needs or teaching skill.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Initiative and negotiation

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy bringing people together to try an idea?
Would finding an agreement between people with different priorities interest you?

facets.interpretation: Starting a shared activity and negotiating are related but distinct; do not infer business management, legal reasoning, sales persuasion or leadership ability from a generic team activity. Law is contextual only, not a direct default interest.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Organization and accuracy

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy organizing information so it is easier to find and use?
Would noticing a small inconsistency and checking it carefully be satisfying?

facets.interpretation: General organization/information accuracy crosses nearly all professions. Office Work is plausible contextual link; accounting requires independent financial interest. Avoid converting liking order into accounting/clerical specialty confirmation or meticulousness ability.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Living systems and stewardship

questions.prompt: Would you want to understand changes in the living world around you?
Would comparing ways to reduce waste or protect a place interest you?

facets.interpretation: Biological inquiry and environmental stewardship are distinct. Living-world curiosity is not agriculture, animal care or clinical medicine. Waste-reduction interest also fits business/design/policy; route through reviewed occupations rather than field keyword assumptions.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation

facets.title: Social systems and fairness

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy understanding why a rule affects people differently?
Would weighing evidence and competing viewpoints about a community decision interest you?

facets.interpretation: Social Science is the closest broad link. Interest in fairness is not proof of legal representation, adversarial argument, campaigning or social-work practice. Separate reasoning about rules from desire to advise/advocate personally.
facets.use: general-interest exploration only; reviewed occupation task links or specific reflection evidence needed for stronger profession interpretation
